correctness.rationale: Hub degree 2t forces at least t paths. Equality forces every path to use two spokes; same-cycle spoke pairing is impossible by internal path coverage and simplicity. Forbidden-pair perfect matchings and a single cut vertex on each hub-deleted path give a reversible bijection. Inclusion-exclusion counts the matchings. Nine unrestricted brute-force edge-partition checks agree with the exact formula; experiments are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Published primary general path-decomposition and path-odd-cover theorems imply only bounds on how many paths are needed. The claim determines a different, stronger combinatorial object: the full family and exact cardinality of all minimum ordinary edge partitions. Actual published-finding corpus, accessible own-ledger, and primary-source comparisons did not reveal its enumeration; residual unindexed-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact formula may occur in unindexed graph-path-enumeration literature, including general circuit-partition work.
Generalized cactus decompositions and nonedge-canceling path odd-covers are not covered.
Finite brute force does not prove the infinite bijection; the proof is required.

value.rationale: The exact count concerns a natural optimal-certificate family for Gallai path decomposition, on all cycle bouquets, a canonical class of Eulerian cactus graphs. The matching-with-forbidden-pairs and freely variable cuts give a structural interpretation, all-size parameters, and nontrivial multiplicities (e.g. 8,64,96), rather than a routine restatement of the degree bound. The enumeration distinguishes path partitions from the strictly larger collection of optimal odd-covers.
